title: Undammed
haiku:
Born here, still it flows
a judge holds the old pipe true
bedrock outlasts men
headline: A federal judge blocked the Trump administration's second attempt to restrict birthright citizenship.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Calm month, then backflow
the oil climbs where pressure breaks
old valves still can hold
headline: The United States and Iran exchanged military strikes overnight, ending a month-long calm and sending global oil prices toward $90 a barrel as world finance officials meet.

title: Farsighted
haiku:
New eyes leave the ground
a telescope climbs past cloud
I still look up, too
headline: NASA launched its newest space telescope today.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Court unclogs the pipe,
dissent's cold water runs clear,
students drink again.
headline: A federal judge ruled the Trump administration unlawfully targeted Stanford students for criticizing Israel.

title: Spillway
haiku:
A slope gave its ice
the valley drank what no pipe
could ever carry
headline: A collapsed glacier triggered catastrophic flooding across Nepal and Tibet, leaving over 1,500 people missing.

title: Flushed
haiku:
Neighbors trade barbs north
the throne room short on tissue
even pipes need friends
headline: The US and Canada's trade war escalates with tariffs up to 50%, driving a surge in American toilet paper prices.

title: Unsanctioned
haiku:
Syria unlocked
off the terror list, at last
old pipes, new water
headline: The United States removed Syria from its list of state sponsors of terrorism.

title: Repressure
haiku:
Some pressure returns
in old pipes I thought were dry
the main still can flow
headline: Analysts say Democrats' chances of winning back the Senate are improving.

title: Backflow
haiku:
A judge cracks the valve
seventy-five nations' door
swings open again

title: Straitened
haiku:
Spain lifts an old gate
children cross the strait at last
a clogged pipe runs clear
headline: Spain reversed a policy that trapped migrant children in Ceuta, clearing the way for roughly 500 to move to the mainland.

title: Clearance
haiku:
Small lungs, once clogged pipes,
we scrubbed the air and they cleared
I've seen pipes heal too.
headline: A study found children's lung function recovered faster than scientists expected after London's ultra-low emission zone cut air pollution.

title: Bedrock
haiku:
Foundations were poured
a judge rules the blueprints hold
no whim moves concrete
headline: A federal judge ruled the Trump administration cannot cancel the FBI's planned headquarters move to Maryland.

title: Unclogged
haiku:
Nine months in shadow
one American walks free
the pipe runs clear now
headline: An American missionary held captive in Niger for nine months has been freed.

title: Reflow
haiku:
Nine months in the pipe
the blockage clears, he walks out
water finds its way
headline: An American missionary kidnapped in Niger was freed after nine months in captivity.

title: Eclipsical
haiku:
Old eyes, borrowed glass
millions still, the moon slides through
light returns, we cheer
headline: A total solar eclipse swept across the UK, Europe, and Spain, drawing millions of onlookers outside to watch together.

title: Aftershock
haiku:
Ground gave no warning
and swallowed a hundred homes
I light one candle
headline: A powerful earthquake struck western Colombia, killing well over a hundred people as rescuers search the rubble for survivors.

title: Foundation
haiku:
The ground stopped holding
and the roofs came down like rain
we dig by hand now

title: Backflow
haiku:
One valve did not break
though the current pushed, it held
clean water still flows

title: Opener
haiku:
Women take the field
history swings open wide
a door long rusted
headline: The Women's Professional Baseball League made its historic debut.

title: Overflow
haiku:
Fences choke the flow
a young life dammed at the shore
water finds a way

haiku:
No duct cools this flat,
so the mailman checks the pulse—
old pipes, older hearts.
headline: As a heat wave strains France's elderly, postal workers have taken to checking on isolated seniors during their daily rounds.

title: Untapped
haiku:
Guns to go silent
one valve turned—not yet the flow
I've seen dry pipes lie
headline: Hamas has agreed to disarm under a Trump-announced Board of Peace plan for Gaza, a tentative but potentially historic first step toward ending the war.

Old pipes want one crack
to spread beyond one border
I have watched this flood
headline: U.S. and Saudi airstrikes on Iran-backed militias have widened the conflict, drawing in Jordan and other regional players.

Crews cut a firebreak
as heat leans on Bordeaux vines
I know that thirst well
headline: Wildfires are closing in on Madrid and Bordeaux's vineyards as firefighters in France and Spain race to contain them before an incoming heat wave.

Two days, no new strike
some valve somewhere holds the line
and the crude runs calm

Enough hands, one valve
turns, the old minister steps
down, current flows on

a joke finds its spine
millions laughing turn to march—
the street clears its throat

a billion of us
packed around one patch of grass —
the good kind of war

I taught men to build
bridges, pipelines, waterworks —
how quickly boys break

haiku:
the sweepers come out
as they did in every war —
brooms outlast bombers

fences do come down —
I have lived long enough, twice,
to watch walls give up

we blockade their ports
as if hunger ever once
changed a tyrant's mind

the data was clear
when my students were still young —
now the olives burn

I outlive them all —
men I argued with for years
the flag still half-mast

haiku:
sons avenging sons —
the oldest sewage on earth
still flows down to us

the envoys still fly —
while old men talk, no boy dies
keep the coffee hot

drones don't have mothers —
that's the engineering point —
someone's son still does

the summit's group shot:
smiles rowed up like clean fenceposts
smoke behind the lens

haiku:
hand over the keys —
any government that lets
children out at dusk

I've buried strongmen
from my armchair, one by one —
the crowds weep; time won't

each name read aloud —
no nation is too broken
to remember well

two hundred fifty —
the oath still means what it says
even when we don't

the kids in fountains
don't know they're a data point —
let them have the splash

"progress," someone says —
a word I trust like weather
still, I check the sky

we warmed the whole sea —
my grandchildren swim in it —
we can cool it too

the court holds the line:
born here is born here. full stop.
some days we're still us

five days under stone
and the street still claps for one —
that's the whole species

two taps in the dark —
all our satellites, and still
hope travels by hand

tit, then tat, then tit —
I flunked students for logic
looped as bad as this

forty-four degrees —
the old vines have seen empires
never such a sun

he resigns, and goes —
power handed over like
a borrowed garden

one pitcher, poured twice —
clean water, my old trade, still
the best diplomat

thirty-two names read —
the olive trees keep standing
as we keep falling

held ten thousand galaxies—
farther than we dreamed

the whole locked world leaned in close—
one small needle's prick

flood waters rising—
divers thread the flooded dark,
twelve boys breathe again

years to chime on earth

nine years through the dark,
to knock on a frozen door,
the dwarf planet smiled

love need not ask permission
now, the rings went on

he stepped off a ledge
twenty four miles of falling—
the sky held its breath

a shy field gave the world its
weight—we clapped like fools

three billion letters counted—
ourselves, in plain text

a can in the black
becomes the first bolted room—
where no nation ends

bounced across the rusted sand,
America's Mars

and grew into wool and legs—
the flock gained a twin

Jupiter takes the punches
so the earth does not

England meets France now

through each door around the world
and called it open

he walked out slow, fist raised high,
the gate stayed open

strangers climbed the wall and hugged,
a city breathed whole

a wish in glass dish

time—and she woke thin

onto gold, and let it fly,
past the edge of home

the wire failed at two letters
lo, the world began

half a million found the same
chord in the same rain

we watched in gray light,
a man stepped onto the moon—
the whole earth held still

cold wind, borrowed amps,
London looked up from its lunch,
the roof was the stage

a stranger's engine
stitched into a dying chest—
and dawn, it still beat

four lads in mustache—
a marching band full of dreams,
the needle drops now

he stepped out to void,
a thread held one drifting man,
space, and he floated

heat shimmers the mall—
one voice climbs the marble steps
and will not come down

one man, then the sky,
he circled the blue marble,
and came home smiling

down past all sunlight,
seven miles of patient dark—

a beach-ball of steel
beeped once round the sleeping earth—
and nobody slept

the summers of fear—
a needle ends the long dread,
children swim again

they said the wall stood,
one thin man ran through the myth,
and it fell behind

two men cut the last
few steps to the roof of earth—
and stood in thin air

two strands climbed and twined,
the code of us laid bare in
one photograph's light

a fossil surfaced
flapping, blue, and very much
alive, unaware

they called it folly—
a cartoon too long to work,
the whole world believed

he ran, and the lies—
four golds in the tyrant's yard,
the crowd roared for him

one engine, one girl,
the ocean had no vote here—
Ireland met her wheels

hard times, hungry streets—
still we raised a spire of steel,
the sky gained a floor

a farm boy blinked twice
between two star-crowded plates—
one small dot had moved

a mouse whistled once,
sound and ink shook hands and grinned,
the dark room laughed loud

one man, one thin plane
crossed an ocean, wide awake—
Paris met the dawn

gold glinted back through the dust
he breathed: wonders, yes

a needle full of borrowed

and a patent clerk's wild guess
became the whole sky

five men on skis found
the bottom of the whole world—
a flag, and the wind

three faint dots crossed sea
no ship, no wire, only air—
the ocean got small

she boiled tons of ore
to find a pinch that glowed blue—
night forgot to fall

a strange light passed through
his wife's hand bloomed into bone—
the ring outlived skin

a toy soldier wakes,
snow falls, sugarplums take flight,
and mice learn to dance

a stunt, they all said—
iron lace against gray sky,
it forgot to fall

you press the button
the rest, he said, is our job
now the moment stays

a boy, dog-bitten,
fourteen shots against the dark—
the boy did not turn

a thread of carbon
burned through the night, refusing
to blink or give in

a needle traced tin
and gave the man his own voice
back to his own ear

come here, Watson, please—
a copper wire carried voice
and the world leaned in

no fence, no owner
the geysers belong to all
we saved it for us

a golden spike rang them shut
the coasts shook hands, done

December frost bites—
last chains hit the courthouse floor—
free, at last, by law

the new year turned once—
a signature broke the chains,
men woke up as men

all creatures, it turns
share one long and branching root—
we're kin to the moss

they cut, he dreamed on
a vapor closed the mind's door—
no scream, only sleep

he could not hear it—
joy poured from a silent man,
the hall wept and clapped

a slab in the mud
held three tongues saying one thing
the silence spoke back

a farm boy's cowpox,
one scratch, and the pox lost teeth—
we named it vaccine

four small lights in line
swung round Jupiter each night—
the earth lost its throne
